Now I see the issue clearly. The agent's `createparser` uses `dest='command'` for the subparsers, so when argparse parses command-line arguments, it stores the subcommand name in `args.command`. 

But the hidden tests call `process(args)` directly with `Namespace(which='compare', version1='1.2.3', version2='2.1.3')` - note the attribute is `which`, not `command`. The test creates Namespace objects directly (not through argparse), and uses `which` as the attribute name.

So the agent's `process` function checks `args.command` but the test passes `args.which`. This is a mismatch between what the agent implemented and what the hidden tests expect.

Let me also check the `test_should_parse_cli_arguments` tests to see what they expect.
